I have farmed this land in Quzhou for over fifty years. My back is not what it was, and my sons have moved to the city, so I manage what I can alone with a little help from my neighbor during harvest. I have about 4 mu of flat, good soil. I know this soil. I am not going to try new things at my age.

I will plant winter wheat in autumn, as I always do. Everyone here grows wheat — it is food, it is reliable, it is what I know how to do. I buy the improved variety seeds from the township supply station, the same ones I have used for the last several years. Not hybrid, just the improved open-pollinated type. I will rotary till after the maize comes off, spread the base fertilizer, then sow. In spring I will top-dress with urea at jointing. I irrigate three times: the winter water before the ground freezes, the jointing water, and the heading water. I do not irrigate a fourth time — my well pump is old and it is expensive. One pesticide spray before heading for aphids, which always come.

After wheat harvest in June, I sow maize directly into the stubble without tilling — my neighbor showed me this saves effort and it works fine. I always use hybrid maize seed,郑单958 or whatever the supply station has that year. Rainfall in summer usually covers most of the water need. I irrigate once at planting if the soil is dry, otherwise I rely on rain. One pesticide spray if armyworm shows up.

I do not grow cotton anymore — the price is uncertain and picking is too hard on these hands.
